chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Uthman ibn Sa'id, from Abdul Kareem, from the people of Hamdan, from Abu Thumamah, who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far the Second (peace be upon him), 'I intend to reside in Makkah or Al-Madina, and there is a debt upon me, so what do you say?' He said, 'Return and pay it to the one who is owed your debt, and ensure that you meet Allah, the Exalted, with no debt upon you. Indeed, the Believer does not betray.'

key_terms.أَلْزَمَ: To reside in / to make a habit of staying
key_terms.مُؤَدَّى دَيْنِكَ: The one owed your debt / the creditor

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on residing in Makkah or Al-Madina while having unpaid debts?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) advises a companion to settle his outstanding debts before residing in the holy cities of Makkah or Al-Madina, emphasizing that spiritual proximity to God requires financial integrity. The ruling highlights the ethical principle that unpaid debts constitute a form of betrayal or lack of trustworthiness, a concept deeply rooted in Shia jurisprudence where debt is a serious right of the people (Haqq al-Nas). This narration underscores the practical implication that one must prioritize clearing obligations to ensure a pure state of accountability before meeting Allah.
